title: The tether and the horse
literal_meaning: According to the stake, the horse leaps.
explanation: The source applies this image to disorder under weak supervision. The horse’s movement is viewed in relation to what holds it, so the remark turns attention from the actor alone to the arrangement around them. In a wider everyday application, repeated disorder may reveal that responsibilities or boundaries have not been made clear. That wider application is editorial; the source does not supply a history of the image.
meaning_odia: ଘୋଡ଼ାର ଡେଇଁବାକୁ ଏଠାରେ ଖୁଣ୍ଟ ସହିତ ଯୋଡ଼ାଯାଇଛି। ଉତ୍ସ ଏହାକୁ ଦୁର୍ବଳ ଶାସନରେ ବିଶୃଙ୍ଖଳା ଘଟିବାର ଅର୍ଥରେ ବୁଝାଇଛି। କେବଳ କାମ କରୁଥିବା ଲୋକକୁ ଦୋଷ ନ ଦେଇ, ତାଙ୍କ ଚାରିପାଖର ବ୍ୟବସ୍ଥାକୁ ମଧ୍ୟ ଦେଖିବାର ଏକ ପାଠ ଏଥିରୁ ନିଆଯାଇପାରେ। ଦାୟିତ୍ୱ କାହାର, କଣ କରିବାକୁ ହେବ—ଏସବୁ ସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ ନଥିଲେ ଅବ୍ୟବସ୍ଥା ବଢ଼ିପାରେ।
usage_example: At a shared event, supplies repeatedly go missing because nobody has been assigned to track them. Someone points to the loose arrangement rather than blaming one volunteer. (Original imagined occasion, not a collected quotation.)
cultural_context: The weak-supervision reading comes from this source’s gloss. Other readings of strength or support are not established here. The comparison is not a recommendation for harsh discipline or a claim that people are animals.
odia_summary: କାମର ଅବ୍ୟବସ୍ଥା ପଛରେ ଦାୟିତ୍ୱ ଓ ବ୍ୟବସ୍ଥାର ଦୁର୍ବଳତା ମଧ୍ୟ ଥାଇପାରେ।
english_summary: The source’s image directs attention to weak supervision behind disorder.
